title: Design a Video Streaming Platform (YouTube/Netflix)
prompt: Design a video streaming platform like YouTube or Netflix. Creators upload videos; the system transcodes them into multiple resolutions, distributes them globally, and streams them to viewers with adaptive bitrate. Also cover metadata, view counts, and a basic recommendations feed. Assume global scale with a very large catalog and heavy read traffic.
blurb: An upload+transcoding pipeline feeding a CDN, adaptive-bitrate delivery, and the read-heavy metadata plane around it.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (upload, transcode, stream/ABR, metadata, search, view counts, recommendations) from non-functional (startup latency, global availability, durability of masters, cost).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about catalog size, upload vs view ratio, live vs VOD, device/codec matrix, target startup time, DRM.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Upload rate, storage for masters + renditions, egress bandwidth (the dominant cost), transcoding compute, CDN cache footprint.

rubric.label: Upload & transcoding pipeline depth
rubric.description: Chunked/resumable upload, segmentation, fan-out transcode jobs per rendition, DAG/queue orchestration, retries, packaging (HLS/DASH). Key senior signal.

rubric.label: CDN & adaptive bitrate
rubric.description: Segment-based delivery (HLS/DASH), multi-CDN, edge caching, origin shielding, ABR ladder, manifest design.

rubric.label: API design
rubric.description: initiate/complete upload, get manifest, playback URLs (signed), metadata/search, view/heartbeat events.

rubric.label: Data model
rubric.description: video metadata, rendition/asset records, upload jobs, view counts; store choices (blob for media, RDBMS/NoSQL for metadata).

rubric.label: High-level design
rubric.description: Write/ingest path (upload→transcode→package→publish) vs read/playback path (metadata→manifest→CDN segments).

rubric.label: Scaling
rubric.description: Elastic transcode fleet, CDN tiering, metadata sharding + caching, popular-title prewarming.

rubric.label: Bottlenecks
rubric.description: Egress bandwidth cost, transcode backlog for viral uploads, cold CDN cache for long-tail, metadata hot keys.

rubric.label: View counts & analytics
rubric.description: Approximate/streaming view counting, dedup, heartbeat-based watch time, hot-video counter handling.

rubric.label: Recommendations
rubric.description: Candidate generation + ranking, precompute vs online, feedback signals; acceptable at a high level.

rubric.label: Observability & reliability
rubric.description: QoE metrics (startup time, rebuffer ratio), transcode pipeline lag, CDN hit ratio, durability of masters.

functional_requirements: Transcode each upload into multiple resolutions/bitrates (ABR ladder) and package (HLS/DASH)
Stream to viewers with adaptive bitrate on many devices
nonfunctional_requirements: Low startup latency (< ~2s) and low rebuffer ratio globally
Durable storage of original masters (11 9s style durability)
clarifying_questions: Catalog size and daily uploads vs daily views?
VOD only, or live streaming too?
Which devices/codecs must we support (H.264/H.265/AV1, mobile/TV/web)?
Target startup time and quality (up to 4K/HDR)?
Are view counts exact or approximate, and real-time or delayed?
qualifying_questions: Do we own the CDN or use commercial multi-CDN?

estimations.traffic: 500K uploads/day (~6/s avg) but each fans out to many transcode jobs; views ~ billions/day, tens of millions concurrent streams at peak.
estimations.storage: Master: e.g., 10GB/hour source. Renditions add ~1.5-2x the master across the ladder. Catalog of billions of hours → exabytes; store masters in cheap cold-ish durable object storage, renditions in warm object storage.
estimations.bandwidth: Egress is the dominant cost: tens of millions of concurrent streams × few Mbps → tens of Tbps globally, served almost entirely from CDN edge to keep origin egress and cost low.
estimations.compute: Transcoding is CPU/GPU-heavy: one upload → N renditions × segments; elastic fleet sized to backlog SLA.

data_model: videos(video_id PK, creator_id, title, description, status, duration, created_at, visibility)
assets(asset_id, video_id, rendition, codec, bitrate, resolution, storage_url, manifest_url)
upload_jobs(job_id, video_id, state, progress, error) — pipeline tracking
view_counts(video_id, count) — approximate, updated from stream
manifests: HLS/DASH per video referencing segment URLs on CDN
api_design: POST /v1/uploads { filename, size, content_type } → { upload_id, chunk_urls } (resumable)
GET /v1/videos/{id}/manifest.m3u8 → HLS manifest with signed segment URLs
reference.high_level_design: Ingest path: client does a resumable/chunked upload to the upload service, which lands the master in durable object storage and enqueues a transcode job. An orchestrator fans the job out into per-rendition, per-segment transcode tasks on an elastic worker fleet (a DAG: probe → split → transcode ladder → package HLS/DASH → generate thumbnails/manifests). On success the video's status flips to published, assets are written, and metadata/search are updated. Playback path: viewer requests metadata + a manifest; the player fetches an ABR manifest and pulls small media segments from the nearest CDN edge, adapting bitrate to bandwidth. The CDN serves ~all bytes; on a miss it goes to an origin shield then the rendition store. Metadata reads are served from a cache in front of a sharded metadata store. View/heartbeat events stream async to an analytics pipeline (approx counting, watch time) that also feeds recommendations.

deep_dives.probe: A creator uploads a 4-hour 4K video and it fails at 90%. How does resumable upload work, and then walk me through the transcoding pipeline — how do you segment, fan out renditions, orchestrate the job DAG, retry failed segments, and only publish when the whole ladder is ready?

How does adaptive bitrate actually work end to end — manifest, segment sizes, the bitrate ladder, and how the player switches? How do you keep origin egress low with tiered caching / origin shield, and how do you prewarm the CDN for a title you expect to go viral?

Your catalog is mostly long-tail. A rarely-watched video is requested and it's not on any edge. Describe the cache-miss path and how you avoid a stampede to origin when a video suddenly trends and many edges miss at once.

How do you count views for a video getting a million views a minute without a hot counter melting down, and how do you dedup a single viewer refreshing? Exact vs approximate, and how do heartbeats give you watch time?

Video metadata lives in your primary store but must reach the search index and the recommendations feature store. How do you propagate changes — CDC/Debezium off the metadata DB vs dual writes — and how do you handle publish-status transitions consistently?
Masters are huge and rarely re-read; renditions are read constantly. How do you tier storage for cost, and what's your durability strategy for masters vs regenerable renditions?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions cdn or cache or edge
followup_bank.question: How do you prevent an origin stampede when a long-tail video suddenly trends and many edges miss simultaneously — request coalescing at the shield, prewarming, jittered TTLs?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions database or store or metadata
followup_bank.question: How do metadata changes reach search and recommendations — CDC/Debezium vs dual writes — and how do you keep publish-status transitions consistent across them?
How do you orchestrate the per-rendition job DAG, retry individual failed segments, and avoid publishing a half-transcoded video?
How do you count views on a viral video without a hot-key counter, and how do you dedup refreshes — exact vs approximate?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions object storage or s3 or blob
followup_bank.question: How do you tier masters vs renditions for cost, and what's regenerable vs must-be-durable?

scaling: Elastic transcode fleet sized to backlog SLA (GPU for heavy codecs)
Multi-CDN with origin shield tier to cut origin egress
bottlenecks: Cold CDN cache for long-tail + origin stampede when a title trends
Hot metadata keys and hot view counters
tradeoffs: Precompute all renditions on upload (fast playback, wasted compute on unwatched videos) vs transcode-on-demand (cheaper, slower first play)
More ABR rungs (smoother adaptation, more storage/compute) vs fewer
Exact view counts (costly, hot key) vs approximate streaming counts
Multi-CDN (resilience, cost leverage, complexity) vs single CDN
Newer codecs like AV1 (smaller egress, higher encode cost) vs H.264 (cheap encode, bigger files)
alternative_solutions: Per-title encoding (optimize ladder per content complexity) vs fixed ladder
Just-in-time packaging (store one mezzanine, package to HLS/DASH at request) vs pre-packaging
P2P-assisted delivery for popular live events
Serverless transcode for spiky small workloads
observability: QoE: startup time, rebuffer ratio, bitrate distribution per region
Transcode pipeline lag and failure rate
CDN cache hit ratio and origin egress
Metadata read latency + cache hit ratio
View pipeline freshness and dedup rate
security: Malware/abuse scanning on upload; content moderation
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer splits the ingest pipeline from the playback plane. Ingest: resumable chunked upload to durable object storage, then an orchestrated transcode DAG (probe → segment → fan out the ABR ladder → package HLS/DASH → thumbnails/manifests) on an elastic fleet with per-segment retries and publish-only-when-complete. Playback: metadata + manifest served through a cache, media segments served almost entirely from a multi-CDN with an origin shield and prewarming, using ABR to adapt bitrate. The candidate calls out egress as the dominant cost and designs around it, handles the long-tail cold-cache + origin-stampede case with coalescing/prewarming, counts views approximately via a streaming pipeline with dedup and heartbeats for watch time, propagates metadata to search/recs via CDC, and tiers storage (durable masters vs regenerable renditions). They name transcode backlog, egress cost, and cold cache as the top bottlenecks with concrete mitigations, and track QoE (startup, rebuffer) as the core reliability metric.

interviewer_notes: Watch for candidates who conflate the ingest pipeline with delivery — the strong ones cleanly separate them. Drive the transcoding-pipeline deep-dive (resumable upload, DAG fan-out, per-segment retries, publish-on-complete) and the CDN/ABR deep-dive (manifest, ladder, origin shield, prewarming) — these carry senior signal. Use the cache/stampede probe on the long-tail cold-cache case and the CDC probe when metadata feeds search/recs. Ensure they recognize egress bandwidth as the dominant cost and reason about storage tiering (masters vs renditions). View-count and recommendations can stay higher level. Reserve the last minutes for QoE observability and durability.
